{"self_assessment": "Impact: I built the bottom line of the fish, the whole lower body outline from the nose joint back toward the tail. That is roughly half of the picture the judge sees, and it is what makes the shape read as a fish rather than a single wavy line. I laid it in steady batches of dominoes, starting as soon as the top line reached the nose. Before the push I inspected the nose and tail area, and the whole fish traced as connected from the start (101 of 101 dominoes). I also fetched a full load of 40 dominoes for the shared bin early on, so the table never ran short of supply.

Execution: I built straight from the scratch pad strokes, which kept the curves smooth and the joints within tolerance. I queued my stroke ahead of time so it began without delay once the top line arrived. In the last minutes I inspected the nose joint closely and checked that nothing stray was connected to it. After that I kept my hands off the nose so nothing could be knocked before the push. That discipline is why the finished piece stayed intact.

Collaboration: I kept the table informed of my progress and said clearly which part I owned, so we avoided duplicated work. I worked with the others' pieces (the top line from Jack, the tail tip from Omar, supply from Hana) and stayed out of their way so we did not bump each other. I also told people when to keep their hands off.

Leadership: When roles needed settling, I confirmed that I held the bottom line, which kept the plan moving. In the final stretch I set the tone for the table: check connectivity, stop touching, and let it run.", "my_share_percent": 30}
